questions.question: According to the second edition of the North Eastern Region District SDG Index (2023-24) released in July 2025, which district recorded the highest SDG score in North East India, with a score of 81.43?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hnahthial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **second edition** of the **North Eastern Region (NER) District SDG Index (2023-24)** was officially released in **July 2025**. It serves as a comprehensive tool to measure the progress of districts across the **eight North Eastern states** in achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
• In this edition, the **Hnahthial** district, located in the state of **Mizoram**, emerged as the top-performing district in the entire region with an impressive score of **81.43**. This highlights the district's significant strides in sectors like **health**, **education**, and **clean energy**.
 
• The index is a collaborative effort between **NITI Aayog** and the **Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)**, with technical support provided by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• Following **Hnahthial**, other high-performing districts in the **2023-24** index included **Aizawl** (also in **Mizoram**) and **East Sikkim** (in **Sikkim**), both of which maintained scores above **78**, showcasing the strong performance of **Mizoram** and **Sikkim** in the regional rankings.
 
• The report evaluates **103 districts** across the region based on **84 indicators** that cover **15 global goals** out of the **17 SDGs**, excluding goals 14 (Life Below Water) and 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) as they are less applicable at the district level in this landlocked region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** These are a set of **17 global goals** established by the **United Nations** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end **poverty**, protect the **planet**, and ensure that by **2030** all people enjoy **peace and prosperity**.
 
• **NER District SDG Index Framework:** This index is the first of its kind in **India** that focuses specifically on a geographical region. It categorizes districts into four categories based on their scores: **Aspirant (0–49)**, **Performer (50–64)**, **Front Runner (65–99)**, and **Achiever (100)**.
 
• **State Performance:** In the **2023-24** report, **Mizoram** and **Sikkim** dominated the list of top districts. **Hnahthial**, a relatively new district carved out of **Lunglei** in **2019**, showed exceptional growth in **environmental sustainability** and **poverty reduction**.
 
• **Regional Coverage:** The index covers all eight states of the **North Eastern Region**, which include **Arunachal Pradesh**, **Assam**, **Manipur**, **Meghalaya**, **Mizoram**, **Nagaland**, **Sikkim**, and **Tripura**.
 
• **Monitoring and Evaluation:** The index allows state and district administrations to identify gaps in **socio-economic development** and helps the **Central Government** in better **resource allocation** and policy framing under the **Act East Policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with First Edition:** The **first edition** of the **NER District SDG Index** was launched in **2021** (for the period **2021-22**), where **East Sikkim** topped the list. The shift in **2023-24** to **Hnahthial** indicates a dynamic change in **local governance** and development speed in **Mizoram**.
 
• **NITI Aayog's Role:** As the premier policy think tank of the **Government of India**, **NITI Aayog** (established in **2015**) uses these indices to foster **competitive federalism** among states and districts.
 
• **Indicators Used:** The **84 indicators** used in the **2023-24** index were refined to include latest data from the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)**, **Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE+)**, and **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**.
 
• **Goal 1 (No Poverty) and Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being):** These two goals saw the highest improvement across most districts in the **North East**, largely due to schemes like **PM-JAY** and **MGNREGA**.

questions.question: The Sachet App, promoted in April 2025, was launched by _______________.

options.text: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Disaster Management Authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, which is the apex body for disaster management in India, promoted and launched the **Sachet App** to provide **real-time disaster alerts** to citizens.
 
• The **Sachet App** is a crucial part of the **Integrated Alert System (IAS)**, designed to disseminate **early warnings** and alerts for various natural hazards like **cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and earthquakes**.
 
• As of **April 2025**, the promotion of this app has been intensified to ensure that every citizen has access to **geo-targeted alerts** based on their current location, facilitating **timely evacuation** and safety measures.
 
• The application was developed in collaboration with the **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT)**, under the Department of Telecommunications, utilizing the **Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)** standards.
 
• The **Sachet App** acts as a single point of information, aggregating data from various disaster-monitoring agencies such as the **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the **Central Water Commission (CWC)**.
 
• A key feature of the app is its **multilingual support**, which allows users across different **states and Union Territories** of India to receive information in their local languages, enhancing the reach of **disaster mitigation** efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):**
 
 
• Established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, the **NDMA** is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• Its primary role is to lay down **policies, plans, and guidelines** for disaster management to ensure a timely and effective response to disasters.
 
• The **NDMA** coordinates with the **State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs)** to implement safety protocols across the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD):**
 
 
• The **IMD** is the principal agency responsible for **meteorological observations**, weather forecasting, and **seismology**.
 
• While it provides the raw data and **weather warnings** used by the Sachet App, it is not the promoting authority of the app itself.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY):**
 
 
• **MeitY** focuses on **IT policy**, e-governance, and the promotion of the **electronics industry** in India.
 
• Though it supports digital initiatives, the specialized **disaster-alerting platform** falls under the functional domain of **NDMA**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• The **National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)** is the premier **policy think tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It provides **strategic and technical advice** but does not typically launch operational public safety applications like **Sachet**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Alerting Protocol (CAP):** This is an **international standard** format for emergency alerting and public warning, which the **Sachet App** uses to ensure consistency across various communication platforms like **SMS, radio, and television**.
 
• **Cell Broadcast Alert System (CBAS):** Alongside the app, the **NDMA** has been testing **Cell Broadcast** technology to send loud, intrusive alerts to mobile phones even without **active internet connections**.
 
• **Geofencing:** The **Sachet App** utilizes **GPS technology** and **geofencing** to ensure that alerts are only sent to people residing in or traveling through the **specific danger zone**, preventing unnecessary panic in safe areas.
 
• **Citizen Safety Features:** The app also includes **educational resources**, "Do’s and Don’ts" for different disasters, and contact details for **emergency services** in various locations.

questions.question: Where was the 71st Senior National Men's Kabaddi Championship 2025 held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium, Cuttack**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **71st Senior National Men's Kabaddi Championship** was held at the **Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium** located in **Cuttack**, **Odisha**.
 
• The prestigious tournament was scheduled for the year **2025**, continuing the long-standing tradition of India's premier domestic kabaddi competition.
 
• The event was organized by the **Odisha Kabaddi Association** under the aegis of the **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)**, showcasing the state's capability to host major sporting events.
 
• This championship serves as a critical platform for players to demonstrate their skills for selection into the **Indian National Kabaddi Team** for upcoming international fixtures.
 
• The **71st edition** saw intense competition among various states, union territories, and departmental teams such as **Services** and **Railways**, featuring top international stars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium:**
 
 
• Located in **Cuttack**, it is one of the oldest and most iconic indoor sports arenas in **Odisha**, with a seating capacity of approximately **6,000** spectators.
 
• Apart from kabaddi, the venue frequently hosts national and international tournaments for **Table Tennis**, **Gymnastics**, and **Badminton**.
 
 
 
• **Senior National Kabaddi Championship:**
 
 
• It is the highest level of domestic kabaddi in **India**, held annually to determine the best state or departmental team in the country.
 
• The **70th edition** of the championship was previously held in **Maharashtra** in **2024**, where the **Indian Railways** team clinched the title.
 
 
 
• **Odisha as a Sports Hub:**
 
 
• The state of **Odisha** has been aggressively promoting sports under its "Sports for Youth, Youth for Sports" initiative, hosting global events like the **FIH Men's Hockey World Cup** in **2018** and **2023**.
 
• The city of **Bhubaneswar** is often called the **Sports Capital of India**, but **Cuttack** remains a vital center for indoor sports development.
 
 
 
• **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI):**
 
 
• Founded in **1972**, the **AKFI** is the national governing body for the sport of kabaddi in **India**.
 
• It is affiliated with the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and is responsible for organizing national championships across various age groups, including **Junior** and **Sub-Junior** levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Player Recruitment:** Performance in the **Senior Nationals** is a major criterion for players to be scouted by franchises in the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, which has significantly increased the commercial value of the sport since **2014**.
 
• **Format:** The tournament typically follows a **League-cum-Knockout** format, where teams are divided into groups (pools) before progressing to the quarter-finals, semi-finals, and the final.
 
• **Dates of Event:** The **71st edition** in **2025** highlights the continued growth of the sport post-pandemic, ensuring a steady pipeline of talent for **India's** dominance in the **Asian Games** and **World Cups**.

questions.question: In August 2025, who among the following was appointed as the Executive Director at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a period of three years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urjit Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the Government of India appointed former **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor** **Urjit Patel** as the **Executive Director** for **India** at the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
• The appointment is for a fixed tenure of **three years**, during which he will represent the Indian constituency at the **IMF Executive Board** in **Washington, D.C.**
 
• The **Executive Director (ED)** at the **IMF** represents a constituency of countries; for **India**, this typically includes **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, and **Sri Lanka**, in addition to the home nation.
 
• The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** approved this high-profile selection to ensure India's economic interests and perspectives are robustly presented at the global lender's highest decision-making level.
 
• **Urjit Patel** succeeds **Krishnamurthy Subramanian**, whose term concluded in **2025**, marking a continuation of appointing top-tier economists to this strategic international post.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urjit Patel**:
 
 
• He served as the **24th Governor** of the **Reserve Bank of India** from **September 2016** to **December 2018**.
 
• During his tenure, the historic **demonetization** of **November 2016** took place, and the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was formally established to target **inflation**.
 
• Before his **IMF** role, he also served as the **Vice President** of the **Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)** based in **Beijing**, focusing on investment operations.
 
• He holds a **Ph.D.** in **Economics** from **Yale University** and has previously worked with the **IMF** in the early **1990s**.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**:
 
 
• Established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**, the **IMF** works to foster global monetary cooperation and secure financial stability.
 
• The **Executive Board** consists of **24 Directors** who are responsible for conducting the day-to-day business of the **IMF**.
 
• The **Managing Director** of the **IMF** (currently **Kristalina Georgieva** as of recent years) serves as the head of the organization and Chair of the Executive Board.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Personalities**:
 
 
• **Krishnamurthy Subramanian**: A former **Chief Economic Adviser (CEA)** to the **Government of India** (**2018–2021**) who served as **Executive Director** at the **IMF** starting in **November 2022**.
 
• **Raghuram Rajan**: The **23rd Governor** of the **RBI** and the first **Indian** to serve as the **Chief Economist** of the **IMF** (**2003–2006**).
 
• **Shaktikanta Das**: The **25th Governor** of the **RBI** (appointed in **2018**), recognized globally for steering the Indian economy through the **COVID-19 pandemic** and global inflationary cycles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The role of the **Executive Director** is pivotal because they participate in the formulation of **IMF policies**, **Article IV consultations**, and the approval of **financial assistance** packages to member countries.
 
• India is one of the **fastest-growing large economies**, and its representation at the **IMF** is crucial for advocating for the needs of the **Global South** and emerging markets.
 
• The appointment reflects the government's strategy of deploying experienced **central bankers** and **policy experts** to international financial institutions to enhance **diplomatic** and **economic leverage**.

6f

questions.question: Which of the following cities served as the venue for the two-day FIBAC banking conference on ‘Charting New Frontiers’, co-hosted by FICCI and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) on 25 and 26 August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The annual banking conference, **FIBAC**, is a premier event co-hosted by the **Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)** and the **Indian Banks’ Association (IBA)**.
 
• For the year **2025**, the conference is scheduled to be held on **25 and 26 August 2025** in the city of **Mumbai**.
 
• The central theme for this two-day event is **‘Charting New Frontiers’**, which aims to explore the future of the Indian financial ecosystem in a rapidly changing global environment.
 
• The venue, **Mumbai**, is strategically chosen as it is the **Financial Capital of India** and serves as the primary hub for major banking and financial institutions.
 
• The conference serves as a critical platform for **Bank CEOs**, **Policymakers**, and **Fintech innovators** to deliberate on strategies for the **Indian banking industry** to support the nation's goal of becoming a **USD 5 trillion economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FICCI (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry)**:
 
 
• Established in **1927**, it is the largest and oldest apex business organization in India.
 
• It was founded on the advice of **Mahatma Gandhi** by legendary industrialists **G.D. Birla** and **Purshottamdas Thakurdas**.
 
• Its headquarters is located in **New Delhi**, and it plays a vital role in policy advocacy and networking for the Indian industry.
 
 
 
• **IBA (Indian Banks’ Association)**:
 
 
• Formed on **26 September 1946**, it is a representative body of management of banking in India operating in India.
 
• It is based in **Mumbai** and currently represents over **240+ banking companies** operating in the country.
 
• The association helps in strengthening the Indian banking system and facilitates coordination between various banks and the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mumbai**:
 
 
• **Mumbai** houses the headquarters of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**, and the **National Stock Exchange (NSE)**.
 
• It is home to the corporate headquarters of almost all major public and private sector banks, making it the most suitable location for **FIBAC**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Participants**: The conference typically features a keynote address by the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and participation from high-ranking officials of the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
• **Technological Focus**: Discussions at **FIBAC 2025** are expected to focus heavily on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**, and the implementation of **Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)**.
 
• **Economic Impact**: The insights derived from the **FIBAC** conference often influence the regulatory roadmap and operational strategies of commercial banks for the upcoming **financial year**.
 
• **Previous Editions**: Past editions of the conference, such as **FIBAC 2024**, were also hosted in **Mumbai** at venues like the **Hotel Trident**, reinforcing the city's status as the permanent heartbeat of Indian finance.

questions.question: In June 2025, which of the following organisations launched NACH 3.0 to enable faster salary and EMI processing?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** officially launched **NACH 3.0** in **June 2025** to revolutionize the bulk payment ecosystem in the country.
 
• **NACH** stands for **National Automated Clearing House**, which is a centralized system used by banks and financial institutions for interbank, high-volume, electronic transactions which are repetitive and periodic in nature.
 
• The primary objective of **NACH 3.0** is to enable **faster salary** and **EMI processing** by streamlining the mandate management system and reducing the settlement cycle.
 
• This upgraded version introduces **real-time mandate** verification and enhanced **API-driven** integration, which significantly reduces the **turnaround time (TAT)** for recurring payments like insurance premiums, utility bills, and loan repayments.
 
• The system is designed to provide a seamless experience for both **corporates** and **retail customers**, ensuring higher success rates for automated debits and credits compared to previous versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**:
 
 
• It is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India, established in **2008**.
 
• It is an initiative of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Indian Banks’ Association (IBA)** under the provisions of the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**.
 
• **NPCI** is responsible for managing several key financial products including **UPI (Unified Payments Interface)**, **RuPay**, **IMPS**, and **Bharat BillPay**.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, following the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• It acts as the **central bank** of India and regulates the entire banking sector and monetary policy.
 
• Headquartered in **Mumbai**, it oversees the **NPCI** to ensure financial stability and security in the digital payment landscape.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI)**:
 
 
• The largest **public sector bank** in India, which was formed on **July 1, 1955**, after the nationalization of the **Imperial Bank of India**.
 
• While it is a major participant in the **NACH** system, it is a user (member bank) rather than the governing body that launches the core infrastructure updates.
 
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**:
 
 
• Established in **1988** and given statutory powers on **January 30, 1992**, through the **SEBI Act, 1992**.
 
• Its primary function is to protect the interests of investors in **securities** and to promote the development of the **stock market**. It does not handle retail payment clearing houses like **NACH**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Advancements**: **NACH 3.0** leverages **cloud-native** technologies and advanced **AI-based** fraud detection systems to ensure that bulk transactions are not only fast but also secure.
 
• **Economic Impact**: By ensuring that **salaries** are credited on time and **EMI** defaults due to technical lags are minimized, this system supports the **Ease of Living** and **Digital India** initiatives.
 
• **Mandate Process**: The transition to **NACH 3.0** allows for the **e-Mandate** process to be completed in **near real-time**, removing the traditional delay of **2-3 business days** associated with paper-based or older electronic systems.
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**: This platform also plays a crucial role in the **Direct Benefit Transfer** mechanism, allowing the government to transfer subsidies directly to the bank accounts of millions of beneficiaries with higher efficiency.
</ul

questions.question: Where was India’s first-ever Astro Tourism Festival successfully held in 2025?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Leh, Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India’s first-ever **Astro Tourism Festival**, focused on celestial observation and the wonders of the night sky, was successfully held in **Leh, Ladakh** in **2025**.
 
• The festival was designed to position **Ladakh** as a global hub for **Astro-Tourism**, capitalizing on its high altitude, low humidity, and minimal **light pollution**.
 
• The event featured diverse activities such as **stargazing sessions**, **astrophotography workshops**, and cultural performances, drawing enthusiasts from across the country.
 
• The initiative is part of a broader strategy to boost **sustainable tourism** in the **Union Territory**, encouraging visitors to explore the unique geographical and astronomical heritage of the region.
 
• It highlights the successful integration of scientific outreach with the tourism industry, fostering **local entrepreneurship** through the training of **"Astropreneurs"** or village-level astronomy guides. ***Hence, the correct answer is Leh, Ladakh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dark Sky Reserve in Hanle:**
 
 
• **Hanle**, located in the **Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Ladakh**, is home to India’s first **Dark Sky Reserve**. This area is strictly regulated to minimize artificial light, preserving the darkness required for high-end astronomical research.
 
• At an elevation of approximately **4,500 meters**, it hosts the **Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT)**, operated by the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Astro-Tourism:**
 
 
• **Astro-Tourism** is a niche form of nature-based tourism that focuses on observing celestial events, planets, and stars in areas with clear, unpolluted skies.
 
• It promotes **eco-friendly travel** and provides a platform for educational science communication, often involving the use of **telescopes** and **sky maps**.
 
 
 
• **Nakshatra Sabha:**
 
 
• **Nakshatra Sabha** is a prominent series of events launched in India (often associated with **Uttarakhand** and **Ladakh**) to popularize **Dark Sky Tourism**.
 
• These campaigns are usually supported by the **Ministry of Tourism** and state departments to diversify the tourism portfolio beyond traditional sightseeing.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Ladakh:**
 
 
• **Ladakh** is often referred to as the **"Land of High Passes"**. Its unique **cold desert** climate and high altitude make it one of the few places in the world with an atmosphere transparent enough for deep-space observation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light Pollution:** This refers to the excessive or misdirected artificial light produced by human activities, which obscures the view of the stars. **Ladakh** maintains a low **Bortle scale** rating, indicating exceptionally dark skies.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By **2025**, the focus on astro-tourism has significantly increased the income of **homestays** in remote villages like **Hanle** and **Pangong**, as tourists seek authentic, off-beat experiences.
 
• **Cultural Connection:** The festival also integrates local **Ladakhi folklore** related to the stars, connecting ancient indigenous knowledge with modern astronomical science.

questions.question: What did the Supreme Court say about Group A CAPF (Central Armed Police Forces) officers in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are part of “Organised Services”**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in a significant observation reaffirmed in **May 2025**, maintained that the **Group A** officers of the **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** are to be treated as **Organised Group A Services (OGAS)**.
 
• This classification as an **Organised Service** is crucial because it grants these officers the benefit of **Non-Functional Upgradation (NFU)**, which helps mitigate the financial loss caused by acute career stagnation. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• By being part of **Organised Services**, officers from forces like **CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP,** and **SSB** are entitled to higher pay scales and better promotional avenues, bringing them to parity with other **All India Services** like the **IAS** and **IPS**.
 
• The court dismissed the notion that these forces are "unorganised," highlighting that their recruitment, training, and cadre management follow the strict protocols of **Organised Group A Services** as defined by the **Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT)**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Supreme Court** emphasized that the nature of duties performed by **CAPF** officers is vital for **Internal Security** and **Border Management**, and denying them **OGAS** status would be detrimental to their morale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF):**
 
 
• The **CAPF** refers to the uniform nomenclature of five security forces in India under the authority of the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**.
 
• These forces include the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**, **Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)**, **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)**, and **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)**.
 
• Recruitment for **Group A** officers in these forces is conducted annually by the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** through the **Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination**.
 
 
 
• **Non-Functional Upgradation (NFU):**
 
 
• **NFU** is a scheme introduced during the **6th Central Pay Commission** in **2008** to address stagnation in various **Organised Group A Services**.
 
• Under this, if an officer of an **Organised Service** is not promoted due to a lack of vacancies, they are granted the pay scale of the higher grade when their batchmate from the **IAS** is promoted to that grade.
 
• The implementation of **NFU** for **CAPF** was a long-standing demand that the **Supreme Court** finally settled in favor of the officers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cadre Review:** The **Organised Service** status mandates a periodic **Cadre Review** (usually every **5 years**), which ensures that the promotional structure remains dynamic and functional.
 
• **Legal Precedent:** The initial landmark judgment for **OGAS** status was delivered in **February 2019**, and subsequent clarifications, including those in **2025**, have ensured that the **Government of India** follows the court's directions without ambiguity.
 
• **Administrative Control:** Despite being **Organised Services**, the **CAPF** remains under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs** rather than the **Ministry of Defence**, distinguishing them from the **Indian Armed Forces**.

questions.question: In January 2025, which of the following Indian institutes/universities was selected as SDG Hub 6 (Clean Water & Sanitation) Co-Chair for the 2025–2027 term?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiv Nadar University, Delhi NCR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, **Shiv Nadar University (SNU)**, located in **Greater Noida, Delhi NCR**, was selected as the **Co-Chair** for **SDG Hub 6**, which focuses on **Clean Water and Sanitation**.
 
• The appointment is for a three-year term spanning from **2025 to 2027**, placing the institution at the forefront of global academic efforts to achieve sustainable water goals.
 
• This designation is part of the **United Nations Academic Impact (UNAI)** initiative, which selects institutions of higher education to serve as **SDG Hubs** based on their research, innovation, and community engagement.
 
• As a **Co-Chair** for **SDG 6**, **Shiv Nadar University** is tasked with leading international collaborations, sharing best practices, and developing academic solutions to tackle **water scarcity** and **sanitation** challenges globally.
 
• The selection highlights the university's dedicated research through its **Center for Public Affairs and Critical Theory (CPACT)** and various engineering departments toward **water sustainability** and **wastewater management**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6):**
 
 
• **SDG 6** is one of the **17 Sustainable Development Goals** established by the **United Nations** in **2015**.
 
• Its primary objective is to **"ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all"** by the year **2030**.
 
• Key targets include achieving universal and equitable access to safe and affordable **drinking water**, improving **water quality** by reducing pollution, and increasing **water-use efficiency**.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Academic Impact (UNAI):**
 
 
• Launched in **2010** by the **United Nations**, **UNAI** is an initiative that aligns institutions of higher education with the **UN** to support and contribute to the realization of **UN** goals and mandates.
 
• It currently comprises over **1,600 institutions** in more than **150 countries** working with the **United Nations** to promote global priorities.
 
 
 
• **UNAI SDG Hubs:**
 
 
• The **UNAI** designates specific universities as **Hubs** for each of the **17 SDGs**. These hubs serve as centers of excellence and resources for other member institutions.
 
• Hubs are chosen for their demonstrated capacity to educate students and conduct research that directly impacts the specific **Sustainable Development Goal** they represent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shiv Nadar University** was established in **2011** by the **Shiv Nadar Foundation** and was one of the first private universities in **India** to be awarded the **Institution of Eminence (IoE)** status by the **Government of India**.
 
• The role of **Co-Chair** involves mobilizing students and faculty to engage in **advocacy** and **policy-making** related to **SDG 6**, ensuring that academic research translates into real-world **sustainability** solutions.
 
• The **2025–2027** term represents a critical period for the **2030 Agenda**, as the world moves into the final five years of the deadline for the **Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
• The inclusion of an **Indian university** as a lead for **SDG 6** is significant given **India's** diverse hydrological challenges and its massive **Jal Jeevan Mission**, which aligns with **SDG 6** targets.
